name: Grain ferment extract

lead: Grain ferment extract is an ingredient in skincare made by fermenting grains like rice or barley and using the resulting liquid in toners, essences and serums.
People use it in the hydrating steps of a routine for softer, brighter-looking skin. It is a category of ingredient rather than one defined compound, so products vary.

paras: Yeasts or bacteria ferment the grain's carbohydrates; the filtered liquid is added to a formula and applied to the skin like any leave-on product.
Generally sold as an ordinary cosmetic ingredient. Allergy to the source grain is the main stated caveat.

chain: Fermented grain liquid is included in a toner, essence or serum
Applied to the face as part of a daily routine
Skin that people describe as softer, brighter and more hydrated-looking
angle.text: People use products containing grain ferment extract in the toner or essence step of a skincare routine, aiming for smoother, more luminous-looking skin. Brands describe the ingredient as hydrating and brightening; these are manufacturer and user descriptions.

lead: Grain ferment extract is a skincare ingredient name used for extracts made by fermenting cereal grains such as rice, barley or wheat with yeast or bacteria and then filtering or processing the result. Products that list it, typically as a named grain plus "ferment extract" or "ferment filtrate" in the ingredient list, are used in toners, essences, serums and moisturisers, where people use them as part of a routine aimed at smoother, more hydrated-looking, more even-toned skin [1].

Fermentation is the long-established process in which yeasts or bacteria convert carbohydrates in a food or grain into alcohol or organic acids; grain ferments in food include sake, beer, kvass, sourdough and rice-and-lentil batters [1]. Cosmetic grain ferments borrow the same idea, applying a fermented grain liquid to the skin rather than eating or drinking it.

The ingredient is not a single defined compound: the contents depend on the grain, the microbe and the process, and brands describe them in their own terms. No published clinical trial of a grain ferment extract as a standalone ingredient is cited here.

paras: A grain ferment extract is made by fermenting a cereal grain or its extract with yeast or bacteria, then filtering or otherwise processing the liquid for use in cosmetics. Fermentation in general is the conversion of carbohydrates by microorganisms into alcohol or organic acids [1]. Ingredient lists name the grain and the word ferment, for example a rice, barley or wheat ferment extract or filtrate.

The ingredient is most often found in leave-on products such as toners, essences and serums used on the face. Proponents and brands associate it with hydration, a brighter complexion and softer skin texture. The exact composition varies between products, since the grain, microorganism and process differ.
As with other plant-derived cosmetic ingredients, people with grain allergies or sensitivities may react to products containing grain extracts; label ingredient lists show which grain is used.
